To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lymphatic drainage system of the testis is composed by three main routes which can be identified by lymphography.

the lymphatic drainage from the testes is directed towards the inguinal lymph nodes in three different pathways, the lymphatics are located in the tunica albuginea of the testes, the lymphatics follow the blood vessels, and the lymphatic vessels in the inguino-scrotal area are not located in the tunics of the spermatic cord.
the lymphatic vessels emerge from the testicular surface in three different groups, which subsequently join to form the two to three main lymphatic trunks of the testes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the lymphatic drainage pattern of the human testis.
the pattern of lymphatic drainage of testis and its implications for the surgical treatment of varicocele.
the basic pattern of the lymphatics of the testes with respect to hydrocele formation after varicocelectomies in adolescents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in adolescents the lymphatic drainage pattern of the testis with regard to hydrocele formation is not affected by the surgical procedure.
the main lymphatic drainage of human testes is via three main lymphatic trunks, which arise from the surface of testes and accompany the testicular artery/vein.
a hydrocele formation following varicocelectomies is not a result of lymphatic damage but a consequence of the surgical procedure itself.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the testicular lymphatic drainage is a complex system of three main routes.
the lymphatic vessels are the most important vessels in the testicular region.
the preservation of one main testicular trunk is the most important factor in avoiding the formation of a postoperative hydrocele.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the testicular lymphatics are located in the subcapsular tissue and that they are located in three groups.
it is possible to identify a lymphatic vessel in the inguinoscrotal region that is the main drainage of the testicular lymphatics.
in adolescents with a varicocele, a testicular hydrocele is a common complication of varicocelectomies.
